title: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot improves topology-optimized structure design
summary: A machine-learning model trained on a synthetic dataset of probable human feedback flags regions of a topology-optimized design that a designer would likely change. The article reports a 39 percent improvement in manufacturability and linear buckling load, adding about 15 seconds of design time compared with all-algorithmic methods. It states the feedback training data is synthetic, editing is limited to thickening or thinning regions, and the approach complements rather than replaces AI-only methods.
ai_technology: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot with topology optimization (machine-learning region-flagging model)

evidence.tested: Demonstrations compared the human-in-the-loop approach with all-algorithmic designs on manufacturability and linear buckling load.
evidence.unknown: No physical testing or real-world construction described. Training feedback is synthetic rather than recorded from real designers.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model quickly identifies design regions a human would likely want to change, within a topology optimization workflow.
